ai.title: Preserve manual edits across chat turns
ai.summary: System prompt injects `changesSinceLastChat` via `gitChangesPrompt` in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. `ProjectFileContextSchema` adds `changesSinceLastChat` record in `common/src/util/file.ts`. `npm-app` computes diffs against `lastFileVersion` using `diff.createPatch` in `project-files.ts`, passed from `client.ts` `sendUserInput`. Scope: Backend prompts, Common schema, NPM app CLI/Client. Detail: `getChangesSinceLastFileVersion` filters null diffs and reads disk content per file path.

eli5.text: When you edit your own files between turns of a coding chat, the assistant will now notice your changes and avoid undoing them. It does this by comparing the file contents from your last chat to whatever is on your disk right now, building a list of your edits, and including that list in the context the assistant sees on its next response. You won't see a new menu or setting; the protection happens automatically each time you send a message while using the local command-line tool.

ai.title: Add recursive directory creation to applyChanges
ai.summary: The `applyChanges` function in `common/src/util/changes.ts` now creates parent directories recursively before writing files. This prevents errors when saving changes to paths that do not yet exist. Scope limited to core file writing logic.

eli5.text: The software now automatically creates any missing folders needed to save a file, so saving your work won't fail just because part of the folder path doesn't exist yet. This applies whenever the system writes changes to disk, and it is live now.

ai.title: Cancel tool-call apply on stale input
ai.summary: Client.ts adds currentUserInputId tracking to guard tool-call subscriptions. Stale responses matching cancelled inputs skip file-change application. Scope limited to npm-app/src/client.ts WebSocket handling.

eli5.text: When you ask the assistant to do something and then quickly ask it something else, the system now ignores the delayed response from your first request instead of still applying it. You would notice that outdated replies no longer make unexpected edits to your files. The program keeps track of which request is the most recent and simply skips any older answers that arrive after you've moved on.

ai.title: Pause mainPrompt after 3 consecutive assistant tool calls
ai.summary: Added a guard in `backend/src/main-prompt.ts` to force a pause after 3 consecutive assistant messages. The change calculates `numAssistantMessages` since the last user message and returns early with a pause response if the count is 3 or more. This prevents the agent from looping indefinitely without user input.

eli5.text: The assistant will now stop and wait for you after it takes three actions in a row without your input, so it won't keep going forever if something is off. Instead of silently continuing, it will pause and tell you it is waiting for more instructions. This affects anyone using the assistant when it would otherwise loop without stopping. It is live today.

ai.title: Patch context matching now allows blank lines
ai.summary: The `findContextMatchTrimmed` function in `common/src/util/patch.ts` was updated to treat blank lines in context as wildcards. Previously, exact whitespace matching was required for all context lines, causing patch failures when surrounding lines differed in indentation or blank status. This change ensures patches apply correctly when context lines are empty, regardless of the target file's whitespace.

eli5.text: When you apply a text patch to a file, the tool now ignores blank lines in the surrounding context. This means a patch won't fail just because a nearby line in your file is empty or has different spacing, as long as the actual code lines line up, it will apply correctly. This makes patch application more forgiving and less likely to break on harmless whitespace differences in the surrounding text. This fix is live today.

ai.title: Move user edit tracking from system prompt to CLI message content
ai.summary: Removed the `<user_edits_since_last_chat>` block from `gitChangesPrompt` in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. The CLI (`npm-app/src/cli.ts`) now calculates changes since the last file version using `getChangesSinceLastFileVersion` and prepends the block directly to the user message content. `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` exports `getChangesSinceLastFileVersion` and refactors the internal logic to support this shift.

eli5.text: You can now see a record of your own edits right in your message, instead of hidden away in the system setup. The tool used to mention your changes to itself behind the scenes, but now it copies them directly into what gets sent with your message. If you look, you'll notice your recent edits appear as part of your message content rather than tucked into the background instructions.

ai.title: Version 1.0.61
ai.summary: Patch version bumped to 1.0.61. Updates `backend/package.json` and `npm-app/package.json`. No functional changes.

eli5.text: The version number shown inside two configuration files was updated from the old value to 1.0.61, but nothing else in the software actually changed. Neither you nor anyone else will see or feel any difference in how the application works today. This was simply a behind-the-scenes label bump to keep the records tidy, and it is live now.

ai.title: Add git commit to bump-version script
ai.summary: The `scripts/bump-version.ts` file now automatically executes `git add` and `git commit` after incrementing the version in `npmAppPath` and `backendPath`. This change ensures version bumps are immediately tracked in the repository history. The commit message dynamically uses the new version from the updated `package.json`. This affects the internal tooling used for release preparation.

eli5.text: When the team prepares a new release, a helper script now automatically saves and records the version number change right after it updates it, instead of leaving that step for someone to do by hand. This live today makes release preparation slightly faster and less error-prone. If you prepare releases, you'll notice the script reports that the changes were committed and no longer requires you to run that final step yourself. This only affects the internal release tooling.

ai.title: Add mapAsync util
ai.summary: Adds `mapAsync` in `common/src/util/promise.ts`. Limits concurrency to `maxConcurrentRequests` (default 20). Resolves with results array.

eli5.text: When the assistant needs to talk to many services at once, it now limits how many it contacts at the same time to 20, so it doesn't accidentally overload anything. The tasks still get done and you get all the answers back in the right order, just without hammering the server with too many requests at once.
